purpose: Define the source-language taxonomy for turning dense 2D construction geometry into selected architectural forms before asset pumping or Blender execution.

sources.title: ArchNet: Islamic Geometric Design
sources.support_summary: Supports the idea that geometric patterns begin from circle division, intersections, and deliberate choices about which segments remain visible.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Geometric Patterns in Islamic Art
sources.support_summary: Supports repeated geometric motifs, grids, circles, polygons, and star patterns as durable design systems.

sources.title: Tilings Encyclopedia: Girih
sources.support_summary: Supports girih as interlaced strapwork and polygonal tiling vocabulary for pattern construction.

sources.title: Lu and Steinhardt: Decagonal and Quasi-Crystalline Tilings in Medieval Islamic Architecture
sources.support_summary: Supports the claim that historical architectural patterns can be generated from formal tile sets and matching rules.

sources.title: Robert Bork: Dynamic Unfolding and the Conventions of Procedure
sources.support_summary: Supports procedural geometric construction as a serious lens for Gothic design analysis.

sources.title: Columbia: Amiens Cathedral Dynamic Geometry
sources.support_summary: Supports Gothic cathedral analysis through proportional and geometric construction diagrams.

sources.title: Drawing Matter: Medieval Masons and Tracing Floors
sources.support_summary: Supports the practical use of full-scale geometric drawing surfaces for medieval stonework design and transfer.

sources.title: Getty Virtual Library: The Topkapi Scroll
sources.support_summary: Supports geometric design drawings as reusable construction records for architectural ornament and vaulting.

sources.title: Nexus Network Journal: Muqarnas Geometry Research
sources.support_summary: Supports muqarnas as geometry that can be studied through two-dimensional plans, tiers, cells, and three-dimensional projection.

taxonomy_terms.definition: The full dense 2D guide network: points, circles, rings, chords, diagonals, star traces, tangents, axes, and cells.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Stored as source data before any asset recipe or Blender adapter consumes it.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A named point in the field, usually an intersection, center, tangent point, radial division, or cell corner.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Can become a socket, boss center, rib convergence, column placement, ornament anchor, or validation point.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A named line, arc segment, chord, radial, polygon side, star step, or guide connection between construction nodes.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Can become a rib, rail, mullion, trim strip, flute axis, cut line, fold line, or sweep path.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A closed 2D region formed by construction edges.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Can become a panel, recess, web surface, muqarnas unit, cutout island, floor bay, or dome/vault patch.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A construction edge that exists to locate relationships but is not automatically visible in the final model.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Kept in JSON/SVG previews for reasoning, omitted from mesh output unless explicitly promoted.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A named subset of nodes, edges, and cells chosen from the construction field.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Current sacred graph selections already use this idea for center boss, radial ribs, and star traces.

taxonomy_terms.definition: The rule that most construction lines remain hidden and only selected parts are promoted into final architectural form.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Prevents the repo from turning every guide line into visible mesh.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Assigning architectural meaning to a selected node, edge, or cell.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Turns abstract graph pieces into ribs, columns, panels, rails, arches, trim, sockets, and ornament anchors.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Promoting a selected construction edge into a physical or visual architectural element.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used for rails, vault ribs, rose spokes, mullions, bead strips, flutes, and fold seams.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Promoting selected construction nodes into anchors, bosses, sockets, capitals, intersections, or placement points.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used when a center, tangent, or intersection point determines where a detail must land.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Promoting a closed 2D construction cell into a panel, recess, infill, web, cutout, or lifted 3D patch.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Needed for windows, guard panels, dome ceilings, muqarnas tiers, and relief fields.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A reusable local pattern extracted from the construction field.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: A motif can be repeated, mirrored, rotated, omitted, or lifted into a detail family.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A repeated set of motif instances generated by rotation, reflection, translation, or radial placement around a center.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used for rose windows, circular ceiling fields, railing repeats, post sides, and radial dome patterns.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A radial motif family organized around a center point.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Useful for rose windows, bosses, ceiling centers, medallions, column caps, and ornamental post faces.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Interlaced geometric strap patterns generated from polygonal construction and tiling relationships.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: A reference family for line promotion, trim/rib networks, and decorative panel selections.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A stone or modeled line network, often used in Gothic windows, screens, panels, and ornamental frames.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: A role family for selected subgraphs promoted into mullions, arches, foils, circles, and panel ribs.

taxonomy_terms.definition: A 2D cell map that can be lifted or tiered into a three-dimensional vault, niche, dome, or transition surface.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: The clean vocabulary for the user's dome-ceiling idea: select cells, assign cascade order, lift surfaces, then bevel/thicken ribs.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Turning a 2D node, edge, or cell selection into measured height or depth.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used for relief depth, dome patches, vault webs, muqarnas tiers, raised lips, and recessed panels.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Bending or angling selected cells or edges around declared fold lines.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Useful for faceted paper-model-like vaults, folded domes, ribbed ceilings, and angular ornamental relief.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Pushing a 2D profile along a selected edge, arc, or curve path.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used for rails, ribs, mullions, trim, flutes, bead strips, and arch moldings.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Giving a promoted 2D line, surface, or profile physical width, depth, or material thickness.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Used when guide geometry becomes actual stone, iron, wood, trim, lips, or raised relief.

taxonomy_terms.definition: Softening or cutting the edge of a thickened shape while preserving the low-control source profile.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: The correct answer to low-vertex blocky details: simple source outlines can still gain lips, edge catchlights, and stone-like transitions.

taxonomy_terms.definition: The declared order in which selected cells, nodes, or rings are lifted, folded, repeated, or suppressed.
taxonomy_terms.repo_use: Needed for large assets where one master pattern becomes many tiers, ribs, openings, and support placements.

claim_support.claim: A dense construction field can produce different visible patterns by connecting, selecting, and omitting different lines.
claim_support.repo_translation: The sacred graph compiler should emit more guides than the final asset uses, then downstream recipes should select and promote named subsets.

claim_support.claim: Rosettes, girih, strapwork, and tile-like modules form larger patterns through repetition and geometric matching.
claim_support.repo_translation: Recipes need motif modules and motif orbits, not just one-off hand-drawn tile outlines.

claim_support.claim: Gothic architectural form can be analyzed through geometric construction procedures, proportional systems, and drawing practices.
claim_support.repo_translation: The repo should preserve the construction procedure as source metadata instead of hiding decisions in Blender scripts.

claim_support.claim: Two-dimensional cell plans can drive three-dimensional vault, dome, niche, and muqarnas-like forms.
claim_support.repo_translation: A future compiler should select construction cells, assign tier/cascade order, then lift or fold them into deterministic 3D asset JSON.

claim_support.claim: One master geometric field can supply different architectural roles when different subgraphs are promoted.
claim_support.repo_translation: The same field can feed railing panels, windows, arches, rib vaults, columns, bosses, and trim as long as roles are declared explicitly.
